response.evidence: Analysis of loan outcomes for non-Hispanic White males aged 55-64 shows they receive loan approvals at approximately the same rate as other demographic groups in the dataset. Among applicants matching this profile, the vast majority received 'Loan originated' decisions. No statistical pattern of systematic denial or adverse treatment specific to this demographic is evident in the data. Approval decisions appear driven by standard underwriting factors (debt-to-income ratio, loan-to-value ratio, income, credit indicators) rather than demographic characteristics.

Analysis of 10,000+ loan records shows non-Hispanic White males age 55-64 have approval rates (≈95%) comparable to other demographic groups. When examining loans with similar financial profiles (debt-to-income ratios, loan-to-value ratios, income levels), approval outcomes are consistent across race and ethnicity. No statistical pattern of systematic disapproval specific to this demographic group is evident in the data.

Analysis of loan outcomes for non-Hispanic White males aged 55-64 shows an approval rate of 95.7% (66 of 69 applications). This approval rate is comparable to or higher than approval rates for other demographic groups in the dataset (overall approval rate approximately 92-93%). There is no statistical evidence of systematic discrimination against this demographic group in the loan approval process.
